instruction: Navigate to the Wikipedia article about Oseltamivir.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to show Tamiflu side effects on drugs.com but encountered Access Denied. Tried medscape.com (Cloudflare 1005), Google search (timed out), then successfully navigated to Wikipedia Oseltamivir article and found the Side effects section.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use Chrome address bar to type URLs, navigate to Wikipedia, click TOC links, scroll through pages, handle access denied errors by trying alternative sites
metadata.failure_analysis: drugs.com blocked with Access Denied, medscape.com blocked by Cloudflare, Google timed out. Model ended on Wikipedia instead of required drugs.com URL.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to direct Wikipedia navigation which the model successfully demonstrated in the trajectory
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the Wikipedia article about Oseltamivir. Evaluator checks active tab URL matches the Wikipedia Oseltamivir article pattern using is_expected_url_pattern_match. [Fixed: changed goto_prefix from 'https://www.' to 'https://' since Wikipedia uses language subdomains (en.wikipedia.org) not www prefix]
fix_history: Fix 1: Changed goto_prefix from 'https://www.' to 'https://' to correctly construct Wikipedia URLs with language subdomains

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction is a single-step task: navigate to Wikipedia Oseltamivir article. Evaluator fully covers this requirement.
Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts Chrome address bar URL via accessibility tree and prepends goto_prefix 'https://' to reconstruct the full URL.
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly receives rules dict with 'expected' key containing regex patterns, and checks all patterns against the URL.
Regex pattern '^https://(en\.)?wikipedia\.org/wiki/Oseltamivir' correctly matches Wikipedia article URLs with optional 'en.' subdomain prefix.
Data flow is correct: getter returns string URL -> metric receives it and regex-matches against expected patterns. No type or semantic mismatch.
